items.title: Pay disputed 'lottery subscription' collection demand
items.quote: Überweisen Sie den Gesamtbetrag innerhalb von 72 Stunden, spätestens bis 06.08.2026, ausschließlich auf folgendes Treuhandkonto: IBAN LT71 7300 0101 2345 6789, Kontoinhaber: A. Petrauskas, Verwendungszweck EC-DE-2026-481120.
items.computation: The letter is dated 03.08.2026 and states a fixed calendar date for payment: 'spätestens bis 06.08.2026' (Thursday). As this is a company (not a public authority), there is no statutory deemed-delivery rule; the date is simply the one printed. No weekend/holiday shift is needed since 06.08.2026 is a Thursday and not a public holiday in NW. Note: this appears to be a fraudulent/predatory collection demand (see warnings) and payment is NOT recommended without independent verification.

warnings: This letter shows multiple classic scam/predatory-debt-collection patterns: it demands payment to a Lithuanian IBAN (LT71...) for an alleged German consumer debt, although the 'creditor' and collection agency both claim a Cyprus address — a foreign account for a domestic claim is a major red flag and should not be paid without independent verification of the payee.

The claimed underlying contract is a 'telefonisch abgeschlossenes Gewinnspiel-Abonnement' (a lottery/game subscription supposedly concluded by phone); such telephone-concluded subscription contracts with consumers are frequently invalid or unenforceable in Germany (e.g. lack of required text-form confirmation under §§ 312a, 312c BGB), so the underlying debt itself is questionable.

The letter explicitly states 'Ein Widerspruch ist zwecklos und verursacht weitere Kosten' (an objection is pointless and causes further costs) — legitimate German creditors and courts never discourage recipients from exercising their legal right to object; this is a pressure tactic to stop the recipient from disputing the claim.

It threatens immediate 'Kontopfändung' (account seizure) 'ohne weitere Ankündigung' (without further notice) if payment is not made within 72 hours; under German law a creditor cannot seize a bank account without first obtaining an enforceable court title (Vollstreckungstitel) via a lawsuit or payment order (Mahnbescheid) — a private debt-collection company cannot lawfully do this, so this threat is very likely false and intended to create fear.

It also threatens an unfounded negative SCHUFA entry and a criminal complaint for 'Eingehungsbetrug' (fraud in concluding the contract) merely for non-payment of a disputed telephone-sales claim; making such threats to coerce payment can itself be unlawful (Nötigung, § 240 StGB) and is a hallmark of scam/fake-inkasso letters.
The extremely short 72-hour payment deadline combined with heavy threats is a classic high-pressure scam tactic designed to prevent the recipient from checking the claim or seeking advice.

Recommendation: do not pay, do not use the given bank details, and verify independently (e.g. via a consumer protection agency, the Verbraucherzentrale, or a lawyer) before taking any action; consider reporting this letter as a suspected scam.
